Hence, the plaintiff has prayed for a decree of permanent injunction, passing off,
delivery up, rendition of accounts, damages etc.
12.

Upon filing of the suit, summons of the suit alongwith notice of accompanying application under Order 39 Rule 1&2 CPC were sent to defendant but defendant did not choose to appear and file WS but sent a letter dt.21.09.2021 addressed to the Court that due to Covid-19 pandemic, he has closed the business for the last several months and will not start business in future. and that he has sent a communication to a Registrar of Trademark seeking to withdraw his opposition vide trademark application no. 4054502.
13.

Finally, on 05.08.2022, as it was found that defendant had neither chosen to appear in the Court nor filed any reply or written statement, so he was proceeded ex-parte and matter was accordingly adjourned for recording of plaintiff's ex-parte evidence to 31.08.2022.
14.

Ld. counsel for plaintiff submitted that despite service defendant has not filed written statement,
therefore, his defence is not on record and hence, judgment may be passed u/o 8 rule 10 CPC.
Thereafter, matter was adjourned for clarification, if any / judgment.
15. I have heard Ld. Counsel Sh. Shayan Khurana for the plaintiff at length and scrupulously and meticulously gone through the record.

16. Order 8 rule 10 CPC provides that "Where any party from whom a written statement is required under Rule 1 or Rule 9 fails to present the same within the time permitted or fixed by the court, as the case may be, the court shall pronounce judgment against him, or make such order in relation to the suit as it thinks fit, and on the pro- nouncement of such judgment, a decree shall be drawn up."
Thus Order 8 Rule 10 contemplates two contingencies, namely (I) where a party from whom a written statement is required under Rule 1 fails to present the same within the time permitted by the Court; and (2) where a party from whom a written statement is required under Rule 9, CPC fails to present the same within the time fixed by the Court.
Under Rule 10, when any party fails to present written statement un- der any of the circumstances stated above, the two courses are open to the Court.
First, the Court may "proceed to pronounce judgment.
Secondly, the Court may make such order in relation to the suit as it thinks fit.

In Disney Enterprises Inc. & Anr. v. Balraj Muttneja &Ors. [CS (OS) 3466/2012 decided on 20th February, 2014], Hon,ble High Court has held that this Court is of the opinion that no ex parte evidence would be required in this matter.

18. Since defendant has not appeared despite knowledge of pendency of the suit, therefore,
contentions of plaintiff as stated in the plaint has remained unrebutted, unchallenged and uncontroverted.

Further defendant has in the letter dt. 21.09.2021 sent to this Court has categorically stated that he has closed the business and not interest in running the business with said trade mark in future clearly proved that defendant has no objection if the relief of permanent injunction as sought by the plaintiff through present suit be granted, hence I allow the present plaint and passed the decree of permanent injunction in favour of plaintiff and against the defendant restraining the defendant by themselves as also through their directors, proprietors, individual proprietor, partners (if any), agents, servants, assigns, representatives, successors, associates,
distributors and all others acting for and on their behalf from using, manufacturing, selling,
exporting, offering for sale, advertising or displaying directly or indirectly or dealing in any other manner or mode in relation to wafers, papads, farsan, different types of snacks, puffed rice, rice noodles, bhel puri, ready to eat cereals, gathiya, popcorn, namkeen, preparations made from cereals falling in class 30 and other allied and cognate goods under the impugned trade mark/ label SOLAR,
trade name M/s. Solar Gruh Udhyog and email id solarnamkeen2020@gmail.com or any other trade mark/name/label identical with and/or deceptively similar to the said trade mark/trade name/label SOLAR of the plaintiff.
19.

Further I pass a decree in favour of plaintiff and direct the de- fendant to deliver of the all impugned finished and unfinished ma- terial with th trade mark/ trade name/ laber "Solar" with in three months.

20. As far as relief of damages is concerned since defendant has not denied the use of trade Mark of plaintiff as evident from his letter dt. 21.09.2021 as he only stated that he has closed the business from last several months.

His letter head contain the name of his firm as "Solar Gruh Udyog" which also clearly proved that defendant was using the trade Mark "Solar" which is registered trade mark of plain- tiff and thus infringed the plaintiff trade mark.
The defendant did not choose to appear and stay away from the present proceedings so as to thwart any enquiry into their account for determination of dam- ages.

As a result, no inquiry into their accounts could be conducted, for this court to pass an order of rendition of accounts of profits and delivery up, so as to compensate the plaintiff for the extent of dam- ages suffered by them.
But, that alone would not be a deterrent.

Merely because the defendant have deliberately elected to stay away from the court proceedings,
cannot be a ground to permit them to reap the benefits of evading the suit proceedings and its Also At vs Shambhu Dhanjibhai Sedani on 10 October, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53828396/
6 outcome.

sentences.text: In my view since defendant is not present no purpose would be served by directing defendant to render its account as he will not render the same willfully and it would be impossible for plaintiff to get the same and thus calculate the profit earned by defendant by selling in- fringed goods.
Hence, I am not passing decree of rendition of ac- counts.

21. The court is mindful of the fact that in such a situation where the defendants choose to stay away from the court proceedings, they should not be permitted to enjoy the benefits of such an evasion.

Any view to the contrary would result in a situation where a compliant defendant who appears in court pursuant to summons being issued, participates in the proceedings and submits his account books, etc., for assessment of damages, would end up on a worse footing, vis-- vis a defendant who chooses to conveniently stay away after being served with the summons in the suit.
That was certainly not the in- tention of the Statute.

Section 135 (1) of the Trademarks Act, 1999 provides that relief that may be granted in any suit for infringement of or for passing off includes injunction and at the option of the plaintiff, either damages or an account of profits.

The plaintiff in the present case has opted for claiming damages and has established be- yond doubt that it has suffered damages on account of the conduct of the defendants which are a result of infringement of their trademark and copyright.

22. It is well settled that damages in cases like the present one must be awarded and a defendant,
who elects stay away from the court proceedings, should not be permitted to enjoy the benefits of staying away from the said proceedings.

In the case of Microsoft Corpora- tion v. Rajendra Pawar &
Anr. reported as 2008 (36) PTC 697 (Del.), considering the aspect of punitive damages, it was held as be- low:-
"22.

sentences.text: Perhaps it has now become a trend of sorts, especially in matters pertaining to passing off, for the defending party to evade Court proceedings in a systematic attempt to jettison the relief sought by the Plaintiff.

Such flagrancy of the Defendant's conduct is strictly deprecatory, and those who recklessly indulge in such shenanigans must do so at their peril, for it is now an inherited wisdom that evasion of Court proceedings does not de facto tantamount to escape from liability.

Judicial Process has its own way of bringing to task such erring parties whilst at the same time ensuring that the aggrieved party who has knocked the doors of the Court in anticipation of justice is afforded with adequate relief, both in law and in equity.
It is here that the concept of awarding punitive damages comes into perspective.

23. Punitive damages are a manifestation of equitable relief granted to an aggrieved party, which, owing to its inability to prove actual damages, etc., could not be adequately compensated by the Court.

Theoretically as well as practically, the practice of awarding of punitive damages may be rationalized as preventing under compensation of the aggrieved party, allowing redress for undetectable torts and taking some strain away from the criminal justice system.

Where the conduct of the erring party is found to be egregiously invidious and calculated to mint profits for his own self, awarding punitive damages prevents Also At vs Shambhu Dhanjibhai Sedani on 10 October, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53828396/
7 the erring party from taking advantage of its own wrong by escaping prosecution or detection."
(emphasis added)
23. In view of above discussion, I held that plaintiff is entitled to damages for infringing trademark/copyright of plaintiff.

Plaintiff has valued his suit for damages for Rs. 3,05,000/- but in my view since no documents has been produced by plaintiff on what basis said damages is calculated and defendant himself admitted to stopped use of plaintiff trade mark, it would be in the interest of justice to grant damages of Rs. 1,00,000/- (Rupees one lakh only)
, therefore, I also pass a decree for a sum of Rs. 1,00,000/- in favour of plaintiff and against the defendant.

The damages awarded shall be payable, within a period of three months from the date of passing of the judgment failing which, the said amount shall carry interest @ 8% p.a. from the date of the decree, till realisation.
24. The plaintiff is also entitled to costs of the suit.
25. Suit is accordingly decreed in favour of the plaintiff and against the defendant with cost of the suit.
Decree sheet be prepared after payment of deficit court fee.
File be consigned to Record Room.
Pronounced on open Court on 10.10.2022 (Sanjeev Kumar Aggarwal) District Judge (Commercial Court)-01, Central, Tis Hazari Courts,Delhi.
